messages:
Maria: Quick ask — I'm putting together a small smoke plan to verify that an on-prem VPC node behaves like our hosted nodes for inference. Can folks skimmable-check this plan and add anything obvious I'm missing? Want to run this tomorrow morning before we flip the canary.

Maria: Proposed quick checks (30–60m total):
- infra: verify MTU, NIC offloads, and kernel netdev settings (rss, tso/gso)
- hw: verify GPU PCIe link speed, NVLINK if present, and GPU driver version
- os: make sure hugepages/hugemem not unexpectedly set, cpufreq governor is performance
- runtime: run 3 short perf runs (1k tokens, concurrency 4) and compare p50/p95/p99 to hosted baseline
- stability: spawn 30-minute continuous stream at low qps and watch mem and fd growth

Maria: Command I plan to run (bench harness):
```
./tools/bench_infer --model redwood-alpha --seq 1024 --tokens 1024 --concurrency 4 --profile latency --out json
```

Maria: Expected quick output snippet to sanity-check:
```
{"p50_ms": 42.3, "p95_ms": 88.1, "p99_ms": 132.7, "throughput_rps": 12.1}
```

Aj: Looks good. Add: check kernel NIC ring sizes (ethtool -g) and IRQ balance pins. We saw mismatches before between cloud images and on-prem. Also add check for network counters increments (rx_drop).

Chris: +1. Also ensure the docker runtime config (if used) has cgroup v2 settings aligned. Our caching layer regresses if cgroup limits differ. Quick command: `cat /proc/cmdline` and `docker info | grep Cgroup`.

Tang: For the 30m soak, can we also attach our tracer to collect 1s-sampled flame profiles? If we get a discrepancy we want to see whether it's kernel scheduler vs. runtime batching. I have a small script: `scripts/collect_flame.sh <pid> 60` that uploads to the perf bucket.

Maria: Good call on flame samples — I'll add that step and the script. Any objection to toggling NIC GRO while testing? We had a case where GRO changed latency shape.

Aj: No objection. Test with GRO on and off (ethtool -K eth0 gro off). Capture p95 delta. Document both results.

Chris: One more: if the node is air-gapped, plumb a small metrics-forwarder to push summary stats to our staging Prom. `agent-lite --push-metrics --endpoint https://staging-metrics`. Otherwise we lose observability.

Maria: s/re: agent-lite — noted. I'll spin that up.

sre-bot: Reminder: please file a runbook note in the eng-runtime wiki under "env-verification-runs" with the run id (will use `env-<ts>`).

Maria: Will do. Plan to tag run id: env-1957212345. I'll paste results in this thread after runs complete. Thanks all :rocket:

Aj: If you want, I can remote into the lab node at 09:00 and iterate live.

Maria: That'd be great, ping me on the call. Thanks!

Chris: TL;DR: infra checks (MTU, offloads, ethtool), kernel/cgroup, driver/GPU checks, runtime bench (p50/p95/p99), soak + flame, metrics push. Looks actionable.

Maria: Final note: prioritize latency percentiles over mean for decision. We'll only escalate if p95 increases >20% or p99 shows desync.
